transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park, Maya Singh, Carlos Lopez, Samira Khan, Emma Chen, Liam O'Neill, Priya Patel, Devon Brooks

Summary: internal enablement — messaging + demo practice. Quick run of elevator pitch, then two role-play demos, then competitor callouts and objection handling.

[00:00] Jordan Park (AE): All right team, thanks for joining. We're 14:00, gonna keep to about an hour. High level: refine the opening pitch, call out the top three competitive differentiators, and run through two short demo role-plays. Maya, Carlos - you two will play SE side and coach on tech points.

[00:25] Maya Singh (SE): Cool. Quick housekeeping, Samira will capture action items and we'll record the demo clips. I'm gonna note places where we should show the Console and the Optimize tab.

[00:41] Emma Chen (AE): Quick ask from AEs — want a 15-sec opener for calls, then a 45-sec for discovery.

[01:05] Jordan Park: Yep. Draft opener: "We help dev teams ship predictable, cost-efficient LLM features across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — so you control latency, cost, and compliance without owning the entire stack." Thoughts?

[01:30] Liam O'Neill (AE): Nice. Maybe tweak to call out "production-grade" earlier.

[01:48] Jordan Park: Good. New line: "production-grade LLM inference" — okay. Maya, Carlos, where do we fold in batching/caching?

[02:10] Carlos Lopez (SE): Short: "We reduce per-token cost with automatic prefix/KV caching and smart batching — your tail latency stays low because of the runtime optimizations." Avoid deep dive on kernels unless asked. Also say "KV cache" not "KV cash" — we've seen auto-transcribe typo in past decks.

[02:33] Priya Patel (AE): Can we have one-liners for Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private? AEs get tripped up on when to push Dedicated.

[02:50] Maya Singh: Hosted = fastest time-to-value, pay-as-you-go. Dedicated = reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, good for sustained high qps. Private = VPC or on-prem for regulated data, brings KMS/HSM integrations. Emphasize rollouts and fallbacks.

[03:20] Jordan Park: Let's do a 45-sec discovery checklist too. Questions to ask: current endpoints (SaaS or self-hosted), traffic patterns, p95 latency SLO, failover needs, compliance/regulatory constraints, budget cadence.

[03:53] Devon Brooks (AE): For budgets, customers always ask for per-token vs per-hour. Any quick guidance?

[04:10] Samira Khan (Sales Ops): Use our cheat-sheet: hosted pricing is per-token, Dedicated is committed monthly capacity — show example math for 100M tokens/month. We'll finalize numbers.

[04:30] ROLE-PLAY 1: PLG Startup (Product demo)

[04:30] Jordan Park (AE, role-play: startup founder): Hey thanks for the time, we're an early PLG company, want LLM chat in-product but super sensitive to cost and latency — what do you recommend?

[04:45] Maya Singh (SE, role-play: customer CTO): So we have bursts during onboarding, and heavy tail queries at night. Latency target p95 under 600ms.

[05:05] Jordan Park: Good qualification. Opening pitch then recommendation: start with Hosted API to iterate rapidly, use streaming and function calling for UX, enable prefix/KV caching to cut repeated token costs, and if you see sustained qps, move to Dedicated to lower unit cost. Also propose a PoC to run a week of real traffic to measure hit rates on cache and tail latency.

[05:40] Maya Singh: Tech callout — we can suggest quantized model variants for cost savings and still keep output quality. Also mention our Optimize suggestions for batching thresholds.

[06:05] Emma Chen: Objection: what about competitors like OpenAI?

[06:15] Carlos Lopez: Answer: OpenAI's hosted API is strong for ease, but Redwood differentiates on deployment parity (same API across hosted/dedicated/private), fine-grained cost controls, and predictable performance tuning. For enterprises, the private deployment story and KMS/HSM integrations are big differentiators versus pure hosted players.

[06:45] Liam O'Neill: Callout — customers ask about model ownership vs serving. Phrase: "We don't claim you need to own models — we enable you to serve them with production economics and operational controls."

[07:05] ROLE-PLAY 2: Enterprise Regulated Workload

[07:10] Jordan Park (AE, role-play: procurement lead): We're a financial services firm, need SOC 2, SSO, private networking, audit logs — can Redwood support?

[07:25] Maya Singh (SE): Short answer: yes. We offer Private deployments with VPC options, HSM/KMS integrations, comprehensive audit logs, RBAC and SAML/SSO. We'll share the security pack.

[07:45] Jordan Park: Customer: what about egress/residency?

[07:55] Carlos Lopez: We support region-specific deployments and can do on-prem bundles for air-gapped needs. Also mention our compliance team can run a design review and checklist.

[08:12] Priya Patel: Objection handling practice: customer: "I need SOC 2 in 2 weeks" — response: timeline depends; we can provide SOC 2 docs if you need evidence, but full org-level certification can't be accelerated; instead offer compensating controls and architecture review.

[08:45] Jordan Park: Good. Let's talk competitive nuance: Anthropic — strong safety and model safety posture; OpenAI — developer mindshare and models; AWS SageMaker/Vertex AI — cloud-first deep integration, but often higher management overhead for inference optimizations. Redwood's angle is production-first runtime + unified interface.

[09:20] Emma Chen: Customers ask about fallbacks — if Dedicated goes down, what's the story?

[09:30] Maya Singh: We have smart routing and automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants or hosted pools. In proposals call it out as "graceful degradation".

[09:50] Carlos Lopez: Also mention canary rollouts, traffic splits, and tracing hooks from Console for debugging.

[10:10] TRANSCRIPT NOTE: audio glitch for ~6s here — speaker overlap, auto-transcript missed a couple words.

[10:20] Role-play continued: cost math example (short): For 100M tokens/month, hosted vs dedicated cost delta shown; Samira to finalize exact numbers in cheat-sheet.

[11:05] Jordan Park: Demo best practices: start with a one-minute customer story, show the Console dashboard (latency/cost per token), then quick live demo of streaming generation with tool-calling, end with a short architecture slide for security. Avoid showing raw infra metrics unless asked.

[11:40] Liam O'Neill: For demos, is it ok to show KV cache stats? Some customers get lost in detail.

[11:55] Maya Singh: Show high-level cache hit rate and explain impact on cost/latency; don't dive into kernel-level stuff unless the SE is present.

[12:15] Jordan Park: Let's practice the 15-sec opener. Emma, you try.

[12:20] Emma Chen (AE - practice): "We help engineering teams ship production-grade LLM features with predictable latency and cost across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — so you can meet compliance and scale without building inference infrastructure."

[12:35] Jordan Park: Good. Tweak: drop 'inference infra' to 'infrastructure' for clarity.

[12:50] Priya Patel: Quick note on refunds and SLA: customers always want to know credits and SLA specifics — Samira, are there standard lines?

[13:05] Samira Khan: Yes, Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets in the contract; hosted has best-effort with higher support tiers. We will produce a one-pager.

[13:25] Carlos Lopez: Tech nuance to prep: if asked about latency below 200ms p95 on long-context workloads, call out model/quantization trade-offs and recommend edge colocated capacity; be honest about tradeoffs.

[13:50] Jordan Park: Ok team, let's go through two demo snippets. Maya, you'll drive the Console view, Carlos you'll narrate the runtime optimization callouts. We'll record both.

[14:00] RECORDING SECTION (approx 10 minutes) — demo walkthroughs, not fully transcribed here due to recording splits, see demo clips in enablement folder.

[24:30] Post-demo feedback:
- Emma: Opening felt long; try to hit pain early.
- Liam: Use a customer metric early to anchor value.
- Priya: Make the security slide a separate appendix, reference during discovery.

[25:20] Jordan Park: Action items recap — Samira capture and assign. We're also going to update the battlecard with a new competitor row for Vertex, and include a short script for the latency vs cost dialogue.

[25:50] Carlos Lopez: I will draft canned responses for questions around KMS, HSM, and on-prem packaging. Include links to the security pack and the private deployment checklist.

[26:10] Maya Singh: I'll record the demo clips and include timestamps so new reps can watch the 90-sec excerpts.

[26:30] Samira Khan: I'll produce the cheat-sheet and update the LMS with the new clips and slide deck. Planned due dates in action items.

[26:45] Final Q&A (crosstalk at times):
- Q: What to do if prospect asks for a hardware spec? A: Ask about qps and sequence length distribution; give a baseline suggestion and follow up with SE sizing doc.
- Q: When to recommend on-prem vs VPC? A: On-prem for air-gapped, VPC for cloud-residency and managed control plane.

[28:00] Jordan Park: Ok wrap. Next meeting: short practice next week, 30 mins, we'll review the public deck and watch the demo clips. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
